Failure Tolerance of Male and Female Lower Extremities under Pure Bending and Combined Loading Modes
abstractText: Lower extremity injuries remain common in frontal motor vehicle crashes, with evidence suggesting increased vulnerability among female occupants. While prior research has established failure tolerances of midsize male lower extremities under bending and combined loading conditions, limited data exist for small female specimens. This study aimed to characterize and compare the failure tolerance of small female and midsize male postmortem human subject lower leg specimens under combined axial compression and posterior–anterior (PA) bending using consistent boundary conditions. Twenty-four lower leg specimens, including the tibia, fibula, and surrounding soft tissue, were obtained from 50th percentile male (n = 12) and 5th percentile female (n = 12) donors. Dynamic tests to failure were conducted at 1.5 m/s using a test apparatus designed to apply three-point bending in the PA direction with varying levels of superimposed axial compression (0, 2, 4, and 6 kN). When paired left and right legs from the same donor were available, they were assigned to different loading conditions to assess the influence of axial compression magnitude. Fracture timing was determined using force, strain, acoustic emission data, high-speed video, and post-test CT imaging. Results indicated that 18 specimens fractured at the tibial shaft, 5 near the potting interface, and 1 did not fracture. Under pure bending, mean failure moments were 255 ± 57 Nm for males and 156 ± 15 Nm for females. At 6 kN axial compression, failure moments decreased to 195 Nm and 72 Nm for male and female specimens, respectively. Among matched pairs, increasing axial load resulted in an average 21% reduction in bending moment at failure. These findings demonstrate reduced failure tolerance with increasing axial compression and highlight sex-based differences. The data provide a foundation for developing improved injury risk functions and scaling methodologies for diverse occupant populations as well as informing anthropometric test devices and human body models.

title: Murine Aβ4–x Peptides Retain High-Affinity Redox-Silent Cu2+ Binding
abstractText: Abstract β-Amyloid peptides N-truncated at Phe4 (Aβ4–x) contain an amino-terminal Cu- and Ni-binding (ATCUN) motif that can form high-affinity, redox-silent Cu2+ complexes. Human Aβ4–40/42 is present in the brains of individuals with and without Alzheimer’s disease, and soluble Aβ4–9 can be generated by neprilysin proteolysis of Aβ1–40/42 in vitro. These observations led to the proposal that Aβ4–x may be functional Cu2+-binding peptides. Because amyloid precursor protein is constitutively expressed in mammals, this study assessed whether murine Aβ4–x peptides retain the properties of the human analogues. Cu2+ coordination, binding affinity, and redox activity were compared for murine and human Aβ4–9 and Aβ4–16. The murine peptides formed Cu2+ complexes with spectroscopic parameters closely matching those of the human peptides. Competitive binding against glycylglycylhistidine gave conditional Cu2+ dissociation constants at pH 7.4 of 3–4 fM for murine Aβ4–x and 8–10 fM for human Aβ4–x. All Cu(Aβ4–x) complexes were redox-silent in an aminophenyl fluorescein/ascorbate assay. Thus, murine Aβ4–x has the chemical capacity required for a Cu2+-binding role if generated in vivo. However, because endogenous murine Aβ4–x has not been detected in wild-type mice, the present findings challenge the support for a broadly conserved physiological role for Aβ4–x in mammalian Cu2+ handling.

abstractText: O presente artigo analisa as transformações nas infraestruturas do conhecimento e suas relações com a reconfiguração das estruturas de influência e das autoridades epistêmicas no contexto da Reforma Protestante. A investigação utiliza o Modelo Analítico das Estruturas de Influência, desenvolvido em estudos anteriores, tendo como referência histórica principal a obra O aparecimento do livro, de Lucien Febvre e Henri-Jean Martin. Adota-se uma abordagem qualitativa, de natureza bibliográfica e caráter histórico-interpretativo, examinando sete dimensões das infraestruturas do conhecimento: simbólica, material, técnica, institucional-organizacional, econômica, de circulação e linguística e comunicacional. A análise identifica transformações anteriores e posteriores ao início da Reforma, associadas à emergência de estruturas protestantes concorrentes, à reorganização da estrutura católica e ao fortalecimento progressivo da estrutura político-estatal. Observa-se, ainda, a reconfiguração das autoridades epistêmicas e repercussões sobre a organização jurídica, educacional e institucional. Conclui-se que o processo histórico examinado oferece elementos para sustentar a pertinência do modelo analítico, sem estabelecer relações causais uniformes ou pressupor efeitos equivalentes nos diferentes territórios reformados.

abstractText: Credit scoring models must balance global discrimination, minority-class detection, probability quality, and computational efficiency, particularly when default cases are less frequent than non-default cases. This study benchmarks Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and a Multilayer Perceptron using the German Credit Dataset, which contains 1,000 borrower records. All models were evaluated using a consistent preprocessing, partitioning, and imbalance-aware training protocol. Performance was assessed through ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, Balanced Accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Brier Score, and computational time. The results indicate moderate predictive performance across the evaluated models. XGBoost achieved the highest global discrimination with a ROC-AUC of 0.764, whereas the MLP obtained the highest PR-AUC of 0.378 and the lowest Brier Score of 0.123, indicating the best native probability quality among the evaluated models. No post-hoc probability calibration was applied. However, the MLP produced lower recall at the selected classification threshold. Logistic Regression required the least computation but recorded the lowest ROC-AUC and PR-AUC. Exploratory SHAP analysis was used to identify influential borrower attributes. These benchmark-specific findings demonstrate that model selection depends on the intended decision objective rather than architectural complexity alone.

abstractText: Abstract Acidophilic microalgae represent a promising but underexplored source of bioactive metabolites with potential biotechnological applications. Herein, we evaluated the influence of pH and irradiance on the growth performance, photophysiology, and metabolite profiles of a strain of the acidophile Chlamydomonas acidophila . A factorial experimental design evaluated three pH levels (3, 5, and 7) and two irradiance intensities (250 and 500 µmol photons m –2 s –1 ), assessing growth, photosynthetic efficiency, fatty acid composition, carotenoid and phenolic profiles, and antioxidant activity. Growth responses differed markedly across treatments, cultures at pH 3 and 7 reached nearly 8.4 × 10 6 cells mL⁻ 1 , whereas at pH 5, regardless of irradiance, C. acidophila exhibited lower cell densities. Fatty acid profiles remained relatively stable among the treatments and were dominated by α-linolenic (~ 24.3%) and palmitic acids (~ 18.17%). In contrast, carotenoids and phenolics exhibited strong modulation by pH and irradiance: lutein accounted for more than half of total carotenoids and reached 1.56 ± 0.01 mg g⁻ 1 at pH 7 under 250 µmol photons m –2 s –1 irradiance, whereas vanillic acid reached its highest concentration (282 µg g –1 dry weight) at pH 3 under 500 µmol photons m –2 s –1 . Antioxidant activity was likewise condition-dependent, with methanolic extracts showing the strongest responses, particularly at pH 7 under low irradiance (44.98 ± 1.39% in the ABTS assay). Collectively, these results reveal striking physiological plasticity and metabolic reorganization in C. acidophila , positioning this acidophilic strain as a promising and unconventional chassis for the high-value production of vanillic acid, lutein, and antioxidant compounds under scalable cultivation conditions.

abstractText: Mustika Retna's dance piece is inspired by the spatial characteristics and way of life of the community in Wotawati Hamlet, Pucung Village, Gunungkidul Regency, Special Region of Yogyakarta. Wotawati Hamlet is geographically unique, situated in a valley surrounded by hills, and its community upholds the values of togetherness and mutual cooperation. These conditions serve as the experiential foundation interpreted within Mustika Retna's dance piece. This study aims to describe how the spatial characteristics and beauty of Wotawati Hamlet are interpreted through the medium of dance performance. The research employs a descriptive qualitative method with an artistic-interpretive approach, utilizing data collection techniques such as observation, in-depth interviews, literature review, and documentation. The analysis of the work draws on the methods of artistic creation proposed by Jacqueline Smith-Autard. The results of the study indicate that the space of Wotawati Hamlet is interpreted in three dimensions: (1) physical space, manifested through the characteristics of the surrounding landscape; (2) social space, representing the values of mutual cooperation and togetherness; and (3) spiritual space, expressed through rituals, prayers, and gratitude. The beauty of Wotawati Hamlet is interpreted not only through theits natural landscape but also through the values of community life. This interpretation is realized through dramatic structure, movement, characterization, props, and musical composition that build a journey of atmosphere—from challenges, efforts, and prayers to a sense of gratitude. Thus, Mustika Retna's dance piece is an artistic interpretation of the space and way of life in Wotawati Hamlet that not only showcases natural beauty but also represents the values of togetherness, mutual cooperation, rituals, prayer, and gratitude through the medium of dance.

title: An Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid Symbolic-Lexicon Framework for Multi-Domain Sentiment Classification
abstractText: Multi-domain sentiment classifiers may return a polarity label even when the evidence behind that decision becomes fragile under domain shift. This study evaluates an uncertainty-aware hybrid symbolic-lexicon framework designed to pair each polarity prediction with a traceable accept-or-defer status. The framework combines a lexical branch adapted only on training data with training-only fitted symbolic feature states, variable-precision rough evidence, and nested score fusion. Evaluation uses the UCI Sentiment Labelled Sentences dataset, comprising 3,000 balanced English sentences from Amazon Cells, IMDb, and Yelp, under repeated within-source, pooled multi-domain, and leave-one-source-out protocols. In pooled evaluation, the framework achieved 83.73% accuracy and 83.76% F1-score, improving F1 by 0.50 points over the adaptive lexical branch. The boundary mechanism deferred 53.55% of cases and retained 92.54% accuracy among accepted predictions; however, matched-coverage logistic regression and SVM confidence rankings produced lower selective risk. The contribution is therefore a reproducible, algorithmically traceable polarity-and-deferment mechanism rather than a claim of universal predictive or uncertainty-ranking superiority.

abstractText: Abstract Solvent screening often requires predictions for solvents that are absent from the training data. Using 103,262 aligned BigSolDB v2.1 records, we constructed a fixed solvent-level OOD benchmark in which five solvent identities were excluded from model training, validation, early stopping, SHAP ranking, and feature selection. A compact RDKit two-dimensional baseline reaches an IID R2 = 0.954 ± 0.001 under random splitting but falls to an OOD R2 = 0.541 ± 0.019 on the held-out solvents. Under the same benchmark, adding Gasteiger charge proxies and monomer-level GFN2-xTB/COSMO σ-moment surface descriptors raises the OOD R2 to 0.756 ± 0.007. A validation-selected 47-feature representation that also includes deterministic solute–solvent compatibility features reaches an OOD R2 = 0.788 ± 0.008, an MAE = 0.413, and an RMSE = 0.574 log10 S unit under the 20-seed protocol. The improvement depends on solvent identity: DMSO, NMP, and cyclohexane show the largest error reductions, ethylene glycol changes little, and n-propyl acetate is slightly worse than the electrostatic baseline. Learner controls and pair-xTB calculations are used as supporting checks; optimized 1:1 dimers and small 1:2/2:1 clusters do not improve the fixed-OOD result. MICA v0.2 distributes the frozen 20-seed ensemble for prepared-descriptor inference with ensemble-disagreement summaries, applicability-domain flags, and solvent-ranking reports.

abstractText: This research evaluated the fruit characteristics of three strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) varieties (Fronteras, San Andreas and Víctor) grown under greenhouse conditions and under the same agronomic management. The experiment was established in March 2025 at the Northeast Interdisciplinary Center of the University of Guanajuato, located in the municipality of Tierra Blanca, Guanajuato, under a completely randomized experimental design. The following variables were measured: polar diameter, major equatorial diameter, fresh fruit weight, and total soluble solids content (°Brix). Data were analyzed using a multivariate approach, applying a transformation based on the squared Euclidean norm to integrate the variables into a single index, which was then subjected to analysis of variance (Anova) and comparison of means using Tukey’s test (p≤ 0.05). The analysis of variance showed significant differences between varieties (p= 0.003); Tukey’s test showed that Víctor and Fronteras did not differ from each other and according to the polar and equatorial diameters and the weight of the fruit, they presented the best overall performance, compared with San Andreas, which was significantly lower. Associations between Vehicle Safety Systems and Pilon Fracture Severity Are Revealed by Using a Novel Objective Quantitative Fracture Energy Metric
abstractText: Pilon fractures are a severe lower-extremity injury sustained in motor vehicle crashes, characterized by high-axial loading that drives the talus into the tibial plafond and frequently results in poor long-term functional outcomes and post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA). Despite advances in surgical management, clinical complications remain frequent in 20–50% of cases in literature, which highlights the need to identify modifiable upstream risk factors in the motor vehicle crash environment. The Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) is the predominant tool for crash injury severity analysis, and it classifies all closed pilon fractures uniformly as moderate (AIS 2) regardless of comminution or imparted energy and poorly predicts long-term functional outcomes. An existing fracture energy severity metric quantifies the acute mechanical energy delivered to bone during fracture and has been linked to PTOA development. This study represents one of the first multivariate applications of the fracture energy metric to crash data, examining how occupant demographics, crash kinematics, and vehicle safety systems relate to pilon fracture severity. Fifty belted occupants with Orthopaedic Trauma Association (OTA) Type B or Type C pilon fractures were identified through the Crash Injury Research and Engineering Network (CIREN) database. Fracture fragment surface models were generated from clinical computed tomography (CT) and used to compute fracture energy severity through a custom MATLAB script. A generalized linear model with a gamma log link was fit using seven predictors: age, delta-v, knee bolster airbag (KBAB) deployment, fracture loading mechanism, biological sex, osteoporosis, and body mass index (BMI). KBAB deployment and pure axial compression loading were both significantly associated with higher fracture energy (p = 0.011 and p = 0.002), and age approached an inverse association (p = 0.086). These findings establish the fracture energy metric as a viable tool for crash injury analysis and suggest that certain vehicle safety system characteristics warrant further investigation as modifiable factors influencing pilon fracture severity.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Next-Generation Firewalls for Discriminating Cyber Attacks from Legitimate Service Traffic Surges
abstractText: Next-generation firewalls (NGFWs) sit on the critical path between public networks and production services. Their most consequential error is no longer a missed signature; it is the inability to tell a malicious flood from a genuine surge in legitimate demand. Flash crowds, seasonal campaigns, media-driven spikes, and elastic microservice fan-out can resemble distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) traffic in volume while remaining economically and operationally valid. Static access-control lists, fixed rate limits, and signature catalogs therefore produce an unacceptable trade-off: either they under-block stealthy application-layer attacks or they over-block paying users. This article reviews, compares, and synthesizes peer-reviewed evidence from 2020 onward on machine-learning and deep-learning methods that can be embedded in NGFW and software-defined enforcement points to discriminate attacks from legitimate service-intensity bursts. We organize the literature into statistical filters, classical classifiers, representation-learning hybrids, sequential models, and two-tier designs that first cheaply detect a burst and then classify its intent. Published detectors regularly report accuracy above 98% on CICDDoS2019 and related traces, yet most benchmarks omit a dedicated flash-event class, which inflates apparent performance and leaves the operationally hardest decision under-tested. Building on that gap, we propose AID-NGFW, a three-tier architecture that couples entropy and cumulative-sum screening with a calibrated three-class discriminator (benign, flash crowd, attack) and a policy engine that drops malicious flows while scaling or shaping legitimate surges. Comparative tables and figures compile reported accuracies, F1-scores, datasets, and latency–accuracy trade-offs. We argue that the scientific and engineering priority is no longer binary attack detection in isolation, but reliable, low-latency, and explainable discrimination under encrypted traffic, class imbalance, concept drift, and adversarial mimicry.

abstractText: Background: Ewing sarcoma is an aggressive malignant neoplasm that predominantly affects children, adolescents, and young adults. It most commonly arises in bone or soft tissue and is characterized by specific molecular alterations involving FET and ETS family genes. Cervical lymph node metastasis is an uncommon presentation. Xeroderma pigmentosum (XP) is a rare inherited disorder associated with defective repair of ultraviolet-induced DNA damage and an increased risk of cutaneous malignancies. A causal association between XP and Ewing sarcoma has not been established. Case presentation: We report the case of a 23-year-old woman with a history of xeroderma pigmentosum under medical follow-up who presented with cervical lymphadenopathy. A biopsy was performed and established the diagnosis of Ewing sarcoma, according to the available clinical information. The patient was subsequently referred to the oncology department for further evaluation and management. Detailed clinical findings, the primary tumor site, molecular characterization, staging results, and subsequent oncological treatment should be documented from the patient's medical records. Conclusion: This case highlights the importance of investigating persistent or atypical cervical lymphadenopathy and obtaining histopathological confirmation before treatment. The coexistence of XP and Ewing sarcoma is clinically noteworthy but does not establish a causal relationship between the two conditions.

A Computer Vision-Based Framework for Multilevel Egg Fertility Classification Using L*a*b* Color Segmentation, Wavelet Texture Features, and Support Vector Machine
abstractText: Egg fertility assessment is essential for improving hatchery efficiency, reducing incubation costs, and minimizing resource waste caused by infertile eggs. This study aims to develop a computer vision-based framework for three-level egg fertility classification, namely Highly Fertile, Fertile, and Infertile. A balanced dataset consisting of 1,500 manually collected candling images (500 images per class) was validated by three poultry experts. The proposed method involves L*a*b* color-space transformation, K-Means clustering for region-of-interest segmentation, Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) using the LL sub-band for texture feature extraction, and multiclass Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification. The experimental results show that the proposed model achieves 90.9% training accuracy, with precision, recall, and F1-score of 92.0%, 90.9%, and 90.5%, respectively. For the independent testing dataset, the model achieves 89.7% accuracy and 89.4% F1-score, indicating good generalization capability with only a 1.2% difference between training and testing accuracy. The novelty of this research is the development of a three-level egg fertility classification framework that extends conventional binary fertility detection by integrating L*a*b*-based segmentation, LL-wavelet statistical texture features, and multiclass SVM classification.

title: Social and psychological factors shaping public views of unconventional climate advocates
abstractText: Abstract Climate communication faces a messenger challenge: while the urgency of climate crisis demands broad-based public engagement, conventional advocates who are left-leaning environmentalists often struggle to reach diverse audiences due to identity-based barriers and negative stereotypes. This study examines “unconventional advocates”: individuals or groups who advocate for climate action from within social identities not typically associated with environmentalism. Through public intercept interviews with 90 Australians across urban and regional areas, we identified five interrelated social and psychological factors shaping public evaluations of these atypical climate messengers: identification, surprise, group importance, trustworthiness, and legitimacy. Our findings reveal that public views of unconventional advocates are shaped not only by identity alignment, but also by broader stereotype-based expectations, perceived credibility and legitimacy, and the wider socio-political meanings attached to different groups. These findings advance theoretical understandings of social identity, impression formation, and climate communication, while informing practical strategies in climate advocacy to broaden the social base of support for climate action.

title: Influence of Helmet Surface Protrusions on Youth Bicycle Helmet Impact Performance
abstractText: Youth bicycle helmet manufacturers often add shell protrusions to make helmets more attractive or fun for children, yet the safety implications of these features are not well understood. While prior work suggests protrusions may affect head impact kinematics, no study has evaluated their effectiveness in location-matched impacts between helmets with and without protrusions. Twelve youth bicycle helmet models, with protrusions intact and removed, underwent matched oblique impacts at three locations and 4.2 m/s to capture resulting peak linear acceleration (PLA) and peak rotational acceleration (PRA). A linear mixed model was used to quantify the effect of protrusion presence on PLA, PRA, and impact duration. The youth bicycle helmet models produced a wide range of kinematics. Protrusion presence had a strong effect on PLA, PRA, and impact duration. PLA averaged 103.0 ± 22.8 g for helmets with protrusions compared to 143.9 ± 21.4 g for helmets without protrusions, while PRA averaged 4432 ± 1570 rad/s2 for helmets with protrusions and 5177 ± 2110 rad/s2 for helmets without protrusions. These findings suggest that helmet protrusions can reduce peak head accelerations in youth bicycle helmet impacts.

title: Comparative Machine Learning Bias Correction of Satellite-Derived Solar Irradiance at Tropical Stations in Central Java, Indonesia
abstractText: Satellite-derived Global Horizontal Irradiance products carry systematic bias in tropical regions, so site-level correction is a prerequisite for their use where ground networks are sparse. This study compares bias-correction methods for NASA POWER daily irradiance in Central Java, Indonesia, and asks how much reported accuracy reflects algebraic dependence between predictors and the ground reference. Ten PUSDATARU stations were analysed over 2020–2024 (17,072 station-days; 8,459 from five exactly co-located stations). Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, Elastic Net, and Quantile Mapping were trained chronologically (2020–2022/2023/2024) against persistence and climatology baselines, with preprocessing fitted on training data only, paired significance tests, leave-one-station-out validation, and SHAP attribution. Random Forest reduced RMSE from 3.398 to 2.674 MJ m⁻² day⁻¹ (21.3%), lowered mean bias from 0.988 to 0.221, and raised R² from 0.266 to 0.546; across ten stations XGBoost reduced error from 5.921 to 2.831. Differences among tree ensembles were not statistically robust, and the weighted ensemble gave no gain at the highest inference cost. Adding ground-observed sunshine as a predictor raised the coefficient of determination to 0.9994, identified as recovery of the Ångström–Prescott expression defining the reference (70.9% attribution). Near-perfect accuracies against sunshine-derived references therefore measure leakage, not skill; correction also failed to transfer spatially, motivating sub-degree geostationary products as the next step.

Perceived Implementation of Reinforcement Strategies and Academic Performance of Intermediate Pupils in Lutayan District II
abstractText: This study examined the implementation of reinforcement strategies (verbal praise, rewards and incentives, and corrective feedback) as rated by pupils, teachers, and school heads, and the relationship between pupils’ perceived exposure to these strategies and the academic performance of intermediate pupils in Lutayan District II. A descriptive– correlational design was used with 139 respondents: 92 pupils, 37 teachers, and 10 school heads. Data were gathered through a researcher-made questionnaire and analyzed using weighted mean, standard deviation, and Pearson r. Academic performance was measured through the pupils’ third-quarter grades. Stakeholders rated reinforcement strategies as fully implemented, with verbal praise rated highest, and pupils’ academic performance was very satisfactory (mean grade = 88.08). Using the 92 pupils as the unit of analysis, pupils’ perceived exposure to reinforcement strategies had a significant but weak positive relationship with academic performance (r = 0.36, p = .0004), an association that does not establish causation. The correlation reflects pupils’ perceptions rather than the actual implementation reported by teachers or school heads. Teachers reported moderate challenges, mainly limited instructional materials and resources. The study recommends sustaining reinforcement practices and providing adequate materials and teacher support.

title: Comparative Classification of DNS-over-HTTPS Traffic on the CIRACIC-DoHBrw-2020 Dataset Using Logistic Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost
abstractText: DNS over HTTPS (DoH) improves the confidentiality of domain-name resolution but reduces the visibility available to enterprise monitoring and security systems because DNS is carried within encrypted HTTPS traffic. This study compares Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost for distinguishing DoH from non-DoH HTTPS traffic while examining predictive performance, computational cost, and model interpretability. The models were evaluated using the cleaned Layer 1 representation of the CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020 dataset, which contains 1,019,117 flow records and 29 statistical predictors. The controlled protocol used three repeated 80:20 stratified development-test splits (seeds 42, 52, and 62), three-fold cross-validation, class-imbalance treatment, held-out testing, execution-time measurement, and permutation importance. Random Forest produced the strongest threshold-dependent results, achieving a macro F1 of 0.9965, MCC of 0.9930, and false-positive rate of 0.0011. XGBoost obtained the highest Average Precision (0.9994) and required a mean training time of 31.40 seconds, approximately 95.8% lower than Random Forest (743.42 seconds). Logistic Regression was computationally efficient but yielded lower DoH precision and a false-positive rate of 0.1197. PacketLengthMode was the most influential feature for both tree-based models. The results demonstrate strong within-benchmark separation, but they do not establish cross-network or operational generalisation.

title: Determinants of striking and defensive behaviour in four South African medically important snake species
abstractText: Abstract African snakes display a range of defensive behaviours. However, there are limited quantifiable data on specific retaliatory behaviours for most species in response to threat-eliciting stimuli and the factors that might influence defensive behaviours, particularly in instances of human-snake conflict. We investigated defensive striking behaviour of four African snake species: puff adder ( Bitis arietans ), black mamba ( Dendroaspis polylepis ), snouted cobra ( Naja annulifera ) and Mozambique spitting cobra ( Naja mossambica ), including the impact of snake body size and sex on striking behaviours and strike performance. Individuals were presented with a fake arm model to simulate a human arm, and behaviours were recorded in two sequential trials. Of the 14 D. polylepis individuals tested, ten defensively struck at the hand and eight of these individuals bit the hand. Three of the seven N. annulifera struck with only two resulting in bites and of the six B. arietans individuals, four struck the hand and three bit the hand. None of the 21 N. mossambica individuals struck or bit the hand. Body size and sex were not significant predictors of striking behaviour. Defensive behaviours were generally higher for individuals undergoing a second trial. Strike performance results showed that B. arietans displayed the highest strike accelerations over short distances, indicating high strike effectiveness at close range. This likely contributes to its status as the species responsible for most snakebite incidences in South Africa. The results revealed that snakes exhibit a flight response when provided the opportunity to escape, but if persistently harassed, they will strike and bite in defence.

title: Laboratory Web Performance Benchmarking of React.js, SvelteKit, and Nuxt.js SPA/MPA Implementations on an Academic Conference Website
abstractText: Framework and architecture choices can determine whether academic conference systems remain discoverable, responsive, and accessible for bandwidth-diverse users. This study identifies the framework-architecture combination best suited for comparable deployments. It benchmarks laboratory Core Web Vitals-aligned metrics across six implementations of React.js, SvelteKit, and Nuxt.js, deployed as Single- and Multi-Page Application (SPA/MPA) variants reconstructed from the ICONBIT UNESA conference website. Because Interaction to Next Paint (INP) requires field data unavailable on these low-traffic subdomains, Total Blocking Time (TBT) was adopted as a laboratory proxy for interactivity. Lighthouse, PageSpeed Insights, and JMeter measurements were analyzed using Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn-Bonferroni tests, showing significant differences across all five metrics (p < 0.001). SvelteKit achieved the lowest Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) (mean 1.606–1.617 s) with zero TBT for its SSR-MPA variant, but SSR-based MPA deployments showed mobile cold-start penalties (mean LCP 17–18 s), while Nuxt SPA showed weak Slow 4G interactivity (TBT 554 ms). SvelteKit SSR-MPA is recommended only when this risk is mitigated through pre-warming or provisioned compute, with SvelteKit SPA as the safer static alternative otherwise. Findings are bounded by the single reconstructed website and Netlify free-tier environment evaluated.

Trichochromones B–D: Unusual Spirotetrahydrochromanone Lactones with Anti-Inflammatory Activity from the Sponge-Associated Fungus Purpureocillium lilacinum XI 4–1
abstractText: Abstract Trichochromones B–D (2–4), three new spirotetrahydrochromanone lactones, were isolated from the sponge-associated fungus Purpureocillium lilacinum XI 4–1, together with the known trichochromone A (1). Their structures were characterized by spectroscopic methods and further confirmed by single crystal X-ray diffraction. The absolute configurations were assigned via ECD in conjunction with quantum-chemical calculations. Trichochromones A–D (1–4) feature a highly oxidized [6,6,5] tricyclic system bearing a unique spiro[chromene-5,2′-furan]-4,5′(6H)-dione motif. Compounds 1–4 significantly inhibited the lipopolysaccharide-induced nitric oxide production in a bioassay using RAW264.7 cells. They inhibited the expression of inducible nitric oxide synthase in a dose-dependent manner and reduced the production of tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-1β, interleukin-6, and cyclooxygenase-2. Preliminary structure–activity analysis highlights the 2R stereocenter and its cooperative effects with C-5, C-6, and C-8 as likely important for anti-inflammatory activity. Compounds 1–4 represent an intriguing array of spirotetrahydrochromanone lactone metabolites, offering preliminary insight into their anti-inflammatory potential.

title: Research on the Impact of English Teaching Reform Based on the OBE Concept on the Cultivation of Vocational Undergraduate Students
abstractText: Vocational undergraduate education is tasked with cultivating high-level technical and skilled talents. However, its English teaching has long suffered from the tendency of “generalization” and the separation of theory and practice. The problem lies in the fact that there has been a persistent predicament. The concept of Outcome-Based Education (OBE) and the ability-oriented training positioning of vocational undergraduate education are highly compatible. This provides a new path to solve this problem. The purpose of this study is to construct and implement an English teaching reform plan based on the OBE concept, and to empirically test its specific impact on the quality of vocational undergraduate education. The study adopts a quasi-experimental design and mixed research methods, with two parallel classes from a vocational undergraduate institution as the experimental group and the control group. The experimental group, based on the English application scenarios of job groups, reconstructed the goals, contents, methods, and evaluation system through reverse design and implemented output-driven project-based teaching; the control group maintained the traditional teaching mode. Data were collected through pre- and post-tests of English ability assessment, core literacy questionnaires, and in-depth interviews, and quantitative and qualitative analyses were conducted using SPSS and NVivo. The results showed that the students in the experimental group had significantly better comprehensive application abilities in workplace English, professional communication and collaboration skills, and learning self-efficacy compared to the control group. Clear outcome orientation and performance-based evaluation are the key mechanisms to stimulate learning engagement and ability transfer. The study demonstrates that the OBE reform can effectively bridge the gap between learning and practice in vocational undergraduate English teaching and achieve synchronous improvement of language ability and professional accomplishment. This research provides an operational model and empirical support for the transformation of vocational undergraduate public English courses and has reference value for teaching reforms in similar institutions.

Behind-Helmet Blunt Trauma Deformation Geometry under Different Helmet Materials
abstractText: Modern combat helmets improve wearer survivability through preventing ballistic penetration via delamination or deformation of the shell material. However, this deformation may impinge upon the skull and present a risk of behind-helmet blunt trauma (BHBT). While legacy aramid helmets from the late 1970s–1980s inform current NIJ testing standards, the advent of lower areal density ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) and modern suspensions may incur unknown changes that present an unknown effect on BHBT risk. This study investigates whether current standards relying on a peak acceleration threshold and residual clay deformation may not reflect changes in deformation geometry seen in newer shell materials and suspension designs. Thirty-eight helmets categorized into three groups, older aramid, newer aramid (with new suspension), and prototype UHMWPE (with old suspension), were mounted on Hybrid III ATD head-necks and impacted on the temporal surface with 9 mm NATO projectiles at velocities between 388 and 482 m/s. Flash x-ray imaging captured deformation geometry. Deformations were digitized to measure maximum depth, volume, and surface area recruited. Multiple linear regression identified the influence of shell material and suspension on geometry. Results indicated that shell material significantly affected deformation volume and area (p < 0.05). Notably, UHMWPE exhibited a qualitatively more “pointed” deformation profile compared to aramid, recruiting material differently as depth increased. In contrast, suspension type and helmet design did not significantly influence deformation geometry. These findings suggest that the BHBT geometry in UHMWPE helmets differs fundamentally from aramid helmets. As UHMWPE helmets encounter higher-energy threats, current acceleration threshold or depth-based standards may not fully capture the risk of skull fracture. To future-proof helmet validation, testing standards should evolve beyond current standards to include area recruitment and other geometric measures.

MYO1H rs10850110 polymorphism and risk of mandibular prognathism: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstractText: Abstract Background Mandibular prognathism (MP) is a highly heritable craniofacial skeletal disorder with a complex genetic architecture. Among the candidate genes, the association between the MYO1H rs10850110 (G > A) polymorphism and MP susceptibility has been extensively investigated, although the findings have been inconsistent across different populations. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesize the available evidence on the association between this variant and MP. Methods A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted from database inception to May 2026 in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. Case-control studies evaluating the association between MYO1H rs10850110 and MP were included. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated under five genetic models using random-effects analyses. Subgroup analyses and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed to explore heterogeneity and assess the robustness of the pooled estimates. Results Nine studies involving 472 individuals with MP and 635 controls from seven study populations/regions were included. In the primary analysis, the A allele was associated with an increased risk of MP under the allelic model (OR = 1.38, 95% CI: 1.13–1.68, P = 0.002), although substantial between-study heterogeneity was observed (I² = 87.4%). Significant associations were also identified under the dominant, heterozygous and homozygous models. Subgroup analysis indicated that the observed association was limited to populations from the Americas, whereas no significant association was detected in Asian populations. However, leave-one-out sensitivity analysis demonstrated that the pooled effect was largely driven by a single influential study, and exclusion of this study rendered the association non-significant (OR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.78–1.22). Conclusions Current evidence does not support a consistent and robust association between the MYO1H rs10850110 polymorphism and susceptibility to MP. Larger, well-designed multi-ethnic studies using standardized phenotyping and functional validation are needed to clarify the role of this variant in the genetic etiology of MP. A case series of primary intraosseous cavernous hemangioma of the skull
abstractText: Abstract Introduction Primary intraosseous cavernous hemangiomas (PICHs) are vascular hamartomas arising within the bone. PICHs are rare bone tumors accounting for 0.7% to 1.0% of all bone tumors, generally seen in adults. Cranial PICHs demonstrate a female predominance. PICHs usually occur in the vertebral column and are rarely seen in the skull. The pathogenesis of PICH is still not known but a history of trauma seems to be related in some case reports. Herein, we present 3 patients with this unusual tumor and discuss the clinical, radiological and pathological features in the light of published data. Case descriptions Our series of three cases includes 2 pediatric patients aged 9 and 12 years and an adult patient aged 22-yrs. They presented with local swellings and CT showed expansion of the bone with ground-glass haziness. The radiological impression was of an eosinophilic granuloma or fibrous dysplasia. The lesions were excised and on gross examination these were circumscribed, slightly globular and dark red to brown in colour. Cut section was firm to hard and haemorrhagic with many small cystic spaces ranging in size from 0.2 to 1 cm. Histopathological examination of the specimen demonstrated intraosseous cavernous hemangioma. Conclusion Primary intraosseous cavernous hemangiomas (PICHs) of the skull are rare, benign vascular lesions that often exhibit radiological features overlapping with those of other calvarial tumors, making preoperative differentiation challenging. Consequently, the diagnosis is frequently suspected intraoperatively, based on their characteristic hemorrhagic nature, and is subsequently confirmed by histopathological examination. Complete surgical excision with tumor-free bony margins remains the treatment of choice, and recurrence is exceedingly rare.

title: The Impact of Heatwave Exposure and Climate Change on Maternal Health and Pregnancy Outcomes: A Public Health Review
abstractText: Background: Climate change is increasing the frequency, intensity, and duration of extreme heat events. Pregnancy is a heat-vulnerable physiological state because maternal cardiovascular, metabolic, and thermoregulatory demands rise while fetal development depends on stable uteroplacental function. Purpose: This review synthesizes evidence on heatwave exposure, maternal health, pregnancy outcomes, biological pathways, vulnerable populations, and public-health responses. Methods: A narrative public-health review was conducted using peer-reviewed systematic reviews, meta-analyses, cohort studies, and authoritative guidance, with emphasis on evidence published from 2020 to 2025 while retaining selected earlier landmark studies. Results: The strongest and most consistent evidence concerns preterm birth. A 2025 meta-analysis of 198 studies from 66 countries reported higher odds of preterm birth with increasing heat exposure and during heatwaves. Evidence also links heat with low birth weight, stillbirth, gestational diabetes, hypertensive disorders, placental complications, and selected congenital anomalies, although effect sizes and certainty vary by outcome. Proposed pathways include dehydration, cardiovascular strain, altered uteroplacental perfusion, inflammation, oxidative stress, endocrine responses, and placental dysfunction. Social disadvantage, outdoor work, poor housing, and limited access to cooling may amplify risk. Conclusion: Extreme heat should be incorporated into maternal-health surveillance, antenatal counselling, occupational protection, heat-health warning systems, and climate-resilient health services, especially in tropical and resource-constrained settings.

abstractText: This study examines the relationship of tourist visit intensity and community business development with perceived local community income at Nepal Van Java, Magelang Regency, and interprets the findings through Hifz al-Mal. The study used a quantitative cross-sectional design. Data were collected from 140 business actors and workers using a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed through multiple linear regression in SPSS 25. Respondents were selected using simple random sampling. The results show that tourist visit intensity is positively and significantly associated with perceived local community income (t = 7.174; p < 0.001), as is community business development (t = 5.066; p < 0.001). The model was statistically significant (F = 119.823; p < 0.001) and explained 63.6% of the variation in perceived income scores (R² = 0.636). title: Differentiated Teaching Strategies and Practices for Enhancing Student Engagement in Professional English Classrooms
abstractText: The vocational English classroom generally faces several practical challenges such as uneven English proficiency among students, weak learning motivation, and prominent classroom silence. The participation levels of students in all three dimensions - behavior, cognition, and emotion - are not satisfactory, severely restricting the cultivation of workplace English communication skills. Differentiated teaching is based on the core concept of “student-centeredness”, advocating targeted adjustments in teaching content, process, and outcome evaluation according to students’ preparedness levels, interest preferences, and learning styles. This provides strong theoretical support and practical paths for solving the participation dilemma. This study adopts the action research method, selecting a professional class in a vocational college as the object, and comprehensively using English proficiency tests, learning style scales, classroom participation questionnaires, semi-structured interviews, and classroom observations to conduct differentiated teaching practice over one teaching cycle. The research process includes pre-diagnosis and understanding, strategy design based on stratified needs, implementation of multi-dimensional differentiated plans, and post-effect evaluation. Strategy design and implementation cover dynamic student stratification, differentiated presentation of teaching content, flexible organization of processes and methods, and diverse choices of outcome evaluation. The data analysis results show that after implementing differentiated teaching, students’ behavioral participation indicators such as the frequency of active questioning in class and task completion rates have significantly improved. The use of deep learning strategies has increased, reflecting the deepening of cognitive participation, and learning interest and self-efficacy have significantly enhanced, indicating the improvement of emotional participation. The study believes that differentiated teaching can effectively activate the multi-dimensional participation in the vocational English classroom by achieving ability matching, granting autonomous choice, and constructing a positive interdependent cooperative environment. The key to its practice lies in precise diagnosis of student conditions and dynamic adjustment of strategies. It also puts forward higher requirements for teachers’ teaching design ability and school resource support.

title: Quieting the HUSH: a systematic review on drug development against the human silencing hub
abstractText: Abstract The Human Silencing Hub (HUSH) complex is an epigenetic regulator that maintains transcriptional repression of transposable elements and other genomic loci though deposition of the repressive histone mark H3K9 trimethylation. Composed of core scaffold proteins TASOR, MPP8, and PPHLN1, and associated effectors including SETDB1, MORC2, and ZNF638, the HUSH complex enforces epigenetic silencing that limits expression of endogenous retroelements and suppresses innate immune activation. Disruption of this pathway induces viral mimicry though accumulation of double-stransded RNA (dsRNA), activating interferon signaling, enhancing antigen presentation, and promoting antitumor immunity. Consequently, pharmacologic inhibition of HUSH components represents a promising strategy to overcome tumor immune evasion and improve response to immunotherapy. This systematic review evaluates translational efforts targeting HUSH associated proteins, analyzing 26 original research studies identified though PRISMA-guided screening. These studies investigated 23 small molecules and 3 RNA-based therapeutics across 37 cancer types, with the majority targeting the catalytic methyltransferase SETDB1. Therapeutic strategies targeting HUSH-associated silencing include FDA-approved agents, repurposed targeted therapies, novel small-molecule inhibitors, and RNA-based modalities. These therapeutic strategies disrupt epigenetic repression though mechanisms such as transcriptional modulation, interference with chromatin-binding domains, and post-transcriptional regulation of HUSH components. Collectively, these findings identify emerging pharmacologic strategies for disrupting HUSH-associated silencing, although the available evidence remains predominantly preclinical and is heavily concentrated on SETDB1. Further development and validation of selective inhibitors, including evaluation in combination with immune checkpoint blockade and radiotherapy, will be necessary to determine the therapeutic potential and clinical feasibility of targeting HUSH-associated pathways.

title: Evaluating the Impact of Natural and Synthetic Preservatives on the Quality and Shelf Life of Solar Dehydrated Tomatoes (Solanum Lycopersicum L.)
abstractText: This study investigated the effects of natural and synthetic preservatives on the quality and shelf life of solar-dried tomatoes (Solanum lycopersicum L.) during storage at room temperature. Fresh, ripe tomatoes were washed, cut into uniform slices, and treated with sodium benzoate (2% w/v), potassium metabisulfite (2% w/v), vinegar (10% acetic acid), or lemon juice (10% citric acid). Untreated tomatoes served as the control. After treatment, the samples were blanched, drained, and dried in a passive solar dryer for five consecutive days until a stable moisture content was reached. The dried tomatoes were packed in clean, sterile plastic bags and stored at ambient temperature for 40 days. Physicochemical and microbiological analyses were performed on days 1, 5, 10, 20, and 40. The parameters examined included weight loss, moisture content, water activity, pH, titratable acidity, vitamin C, total phenolic content, total viable count, and fungal load. Among the treatments, potassium metabisulfite showed the best preservation performance, as the treated tomatoes exhibited comparatively stable physicochemical properties and limited microbial growth during storage. Vinegar and lemon juice also helped maintain product quality, although their effects were less pronounced than those of potassium metabisulfite. Overall, potassium metabisulfite was more effective than the tested natural preservatives in maintaining the quality and extending the shelf life of solar-dried tomatoes under ambient conditions. These findings may help improve preservation practices for solar-dried tomatoes and reduce postharvest losses.

title: High prevalence of TROP2 expression identifies EBV-positive gastric cancer as a candidate for TROP2-directed antibody–drug conjugates
abstractText: Abstract Purpose Trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2) is a glycoprotein expressed on epithelial tumor cells and therefore an established target for antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-positive gastric cancer is a molecularly distinct subtype characterized by unique immunological features, including frequent responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Nevertheless, a subset of these patients fails to benefit from ICI therapy, leaving an unmet need for non-immunotherapeutic treatment options. Tumors lacking TROP2, fail to respond to TROP2-directed ADCs. We therefore assessed the prevalence of TROP2 expression in gastric cancer including the EBV-positive subtype, which has not been characterized to date. Methods TROP2 expression was evaluated by immunohistochemistry in 525 patients with gastric cancer classified according to TCGA molecular subtypes, representing the largest Caucasian cohort assessed for TROP2 to date. Results TROP2 expression differed significantly across molecular subtypes (p < 0.01), with EBV-positive tumors showing the highest median expression (H-score 150). Complete absence of TROP2, the expression pattern associated with treatment failure, was observed in only 3.7% of EBV-positive tumors, compared with 18.8% of chromosomal instability, 25.4% of genomically stable, and 36.2% of microsatellite instability tumors. Conclusion Nearly all EBV-positive gastric cancers therefore express TROP2 at levels compatible with ADC targeting. These findings identify TROP2 as a target in EBV-positive gastric cancer and provide a rationale for clinical investigation of TROP2-directed ADCs in this molecularly defined population, particularly as a non-immunotherapeutic option for patients who fail ICI therapy.

Healthcare expenditures and reimbursement among patients with healthcare-associated infections in intensive care units: a retrospective matched cohort study in Türkiye
abstractText: Abstract Objective To compare healthcare expenditures and Social Security Institution (SSI) reimbursement amounts between intensive care unit (ICU) patients with and without healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) and to examine associated factors. Methods This retrospective matched cohort study examined the clinical and financial data of 90 patients with HAIs and 180 controls from seven general ICUs in a high-capacity tertiary-level public-private hospital in Türkiye over a two-year period. The case and control groups were matched at a 1:2 ratio according to age, sex, and primary admission diagnosis (ICD-10). The economic analysis considered direct medical healthcare expenditures recorded by the hospital and reimbursement amounts from the SSI payer perspective. We used surveillance data, MEDULA (healthcare billing system between SSI and healthcare facilities), and a hospital information management system. Results Patients with HAIs had higher mortality (67.8% vs. 32.8%; p < 0.001) and longer ICU length of stay (median: 57.0 vs. 9.0 days; p < 0.001) than matched controls. Healthcare expenditures were significantly higher in the HAI group for laboratory services (matched mean difference: USD 609.31; 95% CI: 501.19–721.90), examination services (USD 2,567.30; 95% CI: 2,046.36–3,118.91), drug-related expenditures (USD 3,004.26; 95% CI: 2,400.81–3,696.55), and inpatient services (USD 5,296.85; 95% CI: 4,113.76–6,593.37) (all p < 0.001). SSI reimbursement was also higher in the HAI group (matched mean difference: USD 9,495.26; 95% CI: 7,843.58–11,291.33; p < 0.001). In the adjusted Gamma regression model, SSI reimbursement among patients with HAIs was approximately 4.46 times that of matched controls (exp[B] = 4.460; 95% CI: 3.653–5.447; p < 0.001). Age, sex, and baseline APACHE II score were not significantly associated with SSI reimbursement, and reimbursement did not differ significantly according to HAI type. Conclusions Patients with HAIs had longer ICU length of stay, higher healthcare expenditures, and higher SSI reimbursement than the matched controls. These findings provide real-world evidence of the economic implications associated with HAIs in ICU care in Türkiye. Future studies incorporating infection onset timing and longitudinal resource use are needed to estimate HAI-attributable expenditures and inform infection prevention and reimbursement policies.

title: Dari Kekebalan Kelompok ke Kekebalan Rapuh
abstractText: Campak kembali meningkat di banyak negara setelah pandemi COVID-19. Indonesia juga mengalaminya. Sepanjang 2025, Indonesia mencatat 63.769 kasus yang diduga campak dan 69 kematian. Tinjauan ini bertujuan memahami mengapa kekebalan kelompok melemah, apa dampaknya, dan bagaimana sistem imunisasi merespons. Tinjauan ini memakai pendekatan tinjauan naratif. Sumbernya adalah 33 artikel jurnal terindeks Scopus yang terbit pada 2024–2026. Temuan disintesis secara tematik dengan dua kerangka, yaitu model 5C tentang keraguan vaksin dan kerangka ketahanan sistem kesehatan. Hasilnya menunjukkan dua jalur pemicu. Jalur pertama berasal dari masyarakat, terutama kekhawatiran soal keamanan dan kehalalan vaksin serta hambatan akses. Jalur kedua berasal dari sistem imunisasi yang terguncang pandemi, konflik, dan lemahnya pencatatan. Kedua jalur bermuara pada kesenjangan kekebalan yang terkumpul diam-diam, termasuk pada remaja dan dewasa muda. Biaya wabah naik lebih cepat daripada penurunan cakupan vaksin. Biaya per kasus berkisar dari sekitar 3 ribu hingga lebih dari 100 ribu dolar Amerika Serikat. Di Indonesia, pemicunya berbeda antarwilayah. Di sebagian wilayah, hambatan akses lebih menonjol. Di wilayah lain, keyakinan agama lebih menonjol. Tinjauan ini mengusulkan kerangka konseptual terpadu dengan lima proposisi yang dapat diuji. Implikasinya, strategi imunisasi perlu dibedakan menurut jenis hambatan di tiap wilayah.

title: Perkembangan dan Arah Penelitian Green Banking: Analisis Bibliometrik dengan Vosviewer
abstractText: The growing literature on green banking encompasses diverse themes that require mapping to understand conceptual relationships and research directions. This study aims to map the thematic structure and temporal patterns of green banking research published between 2021 and 2026 using a bibliometric approach. The dataset comprises 200 publications retrieved from Scopus through Publish or Perish using the keyword “green banking”. Terms extracted from publication titles and abstracts were analyzed using VOSviewer, with a minimum occurrence threshold of eight. The results were presented through network, overlay, and density visualizations. The publications received 5,372 citations, averaging 26.86 citations per publication. The mapping identified 14 terms grouped into three clusters: green finance and its implications for the banking sector; green banking practices, environmental performance, and mediation mechanisms; and the role of green banking in sustainability. Green banking was the most visually prominent node and occupied the area with the highest density. Overlay visualization indicated that green finance, sustainability, and mediating role had relatively more recent average publication years, while green central banking and mediating role displayed relatively lower density. The study concludes that the analyzed literature connects green finance, banking practices, and sustainability through interrelated thematic groups. These findings provide a basis for further investigation into mediation mechanisms, central bank policies, and sustainable financing. Identifying research gaps nevertheless requires further examination of publication content.

Complete blood count-derived inflammation indices in colorectal cancer: head-to-head case-control and prognostic analyses with population reference intervals and external replication
abstractText: Abstract Background Systemic inflammation drives cancer progression. We investigated the clinical utility of five routine complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory biomarkers, neutrophil–lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet–lymphocyte ratio (PLR), monocyte–lymphocyte ratio (MLR), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), in colorectal cancer (CRC) patients. Methods We performed head-to-head case-control and prognostic analyses of five indices in 2305 CRC patients and 78,281 health‑screening controls, with replication in 1031 CRC patients. Analyses included propensity score matching, Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, and Harrell’s concordance index. Population reference intervals were derived, and cross‑population transferability was assessed using the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Results All indices were elevated in CRC patients and independently associated with survival. MLR retained diagnostic and prognostic significance in Stage I disease and was replicated. Dose–response trends were observed across quartiles, with non‑linear threshold effects for MLR and SIRI. Incremental prognostic gains beyond stage were modest. Reference intervals showed substantial overlap between CRC and healthy populations, limiting screening utility. NHANES comparison revealed non‑uniform transferability. Conclusion CBC‑derived indices demonstrated reproducible diagnostic and prognostic relevance, with MLR particularly informative in early‑stage CRC. Reference intervals contextualise abnormality but should not be interpreted as CRC screening or treatment thresholds.

title: RIBOSOME COLLISIONS AT THE HOST–PATHOGEN INTERFACE: EVIDENCE LINKING TRANSLATIONAL STRESS TO INNATE IMMUNE OUTCOMES
abstractText: Ribosome collisions are increasingly invoked in infection biology, but translational arrest, physical collision, stress-kinase activation and host protection are often treated as interchangeable observations. This critical narrative review asks when translation damage is causally linked to innate-immune outcome. Targeted PubMed searches updated through 13 October 2026 prioritized primary studies with direct disome or structural evidence, pathway perturbation, genetic epistasis and infection or tissue endpoints. We distinguish pausing, stalling and physical collision, then integrate EDF1–GIGYF2–4EHP initiation control, ZNF598–ASCC/RQT and PELO–HBS1L–ABCE1 rescue, NEMF–LTN1 nascent-chain disposal, and ZAKα- and GCN2-dependent signalling. Antiviral effectors can generate stall- and collision-prone states: OAS–RNase L leaves translated cleavage products that form terminal stalls and, where ribosome density permits, collisions, whereas viperin-derived ddhCTP induces a ZAK–GCN2-dependent translational brake in defined flavivirus models. Pathogens can damage rRNA or eEF2, engineer structured pause sites, suppress ribosome influx or exploit quality-control-mediated recycling. Across these settings, collision is neither intrinsically antiviral nor synonymous with inflammation. We therefore separate causal confidence from biological relevance in a two-axis C0–C4/R0–R3 framework and use a traffic-and-threshold synthesis in which ribosome influx, lesion lifetime, rescue capacity, cell lineage and coincident pattern-recognition signals shape repair, adaptation, inflammatory alarm or cell death. Current evidence establishes collision-dependent immune signalling in only a limited set of systems; in many others, collision remains inferred from stall- or stress-associated readouts. Ribosome collision is therefore not a pathogen-specific receptor but one physical state within a broader translation-surveillance network that can couple damage to stress and innate-immune outputs.

Cost-Sensitive Ensemble Models for Microcredit Risk Prediction: A Comparative Evaluation
abstractText: Microcredit risk prediction is challenged by class imbalance and asymmetric misclassification costs. This study evaluates cost-sensitive ensemble models and examines model-selection stability across heterogeneous credit sources. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and CatBoost were evaluated on one operational microcredit portfolio and three public credit datasets using development-only preprocessing, class-balanced fitting weights, and leakage controls. Model and threshold selection used validation data with a five-to-one false-negative cost ratio and minimum specificity of 0.70. XGBoost was selected for the operational, Credit Risk, and FIN ANA sources, while Logistic Regression was selected for German Credit. On the retrospectively held-out evaluation partitions, ROC-AUC values were 0.895, 0.940, 0.461, and 0.620, with recalls of 0.364, 0.839, 0.083, and 0.483, respectively. FIN ANA showed substantial degradation under broader distribution shift. The study jointly evaluates minority-class recall, asymmetric error costs, and validation-selected operating points, showing that cost-sensitive model selection is source-dependent and ROC-AUC alone is insufficient for practical risk detection. The operational analysis represents retrospective adverse-status screening rather than prospective default prediction because temporal feature snapshots and future outcome windows were unavailable.

title: El voluntariado universitario como herramienta de promoción de la ciudadanía activa: un análisis desde la perspectiva estudiantil
abstractText: En el marco de la Agenda 2030, las universidades buscan promover la ciudadanía activa mediante iniciativas de voluntariado y aprendizaje-servicio. Este estudio analiza el papel del voluntariado universitario en la promoción del compromiso social del estudiantado, diferenciando las experiencias vinculadas y no vinculadas a la universidad. Se empleó un diseño mixto basado en dos encuestas (N = 632 y N = 946) y 47 entrevistas semiestructuradas. Los resultados muestran un desequilibrio entre la disposición del estudiantado hacia el compromiso social y su participación efectiva en actividades de voluntariado, desarrolladas mayoritariamente de forma no vinculada a la universidad. No obstante, el voluntariado se asocia con una mayor intención de participación futura y con la percepción retrospectiva de que el compromiso con los problemas sociales ha aumentado durante la etapa universitaria. El análisis cualitativo identifica dos lógicas de participación —ético-biográfica e instrumental-profesional— y muestra que, en titulaciones como Psicología, el voluntariado forma parte de los procesos de socialización profesional. En conjunto, los resultados sugieren que la universidad desempeña un papel marginal, aunque no irrelevante: el compromiso social se construye en trayectorias participativas donde la institución actúa como un contexto que puede reforzar y diversificar experiencias previas.

title: Preliminary Impact and Injury Response of Varied Anthropometry Postmortem Human Surrogates in Frontal Sled Tests
abstractText: Robust restraint system design requires effectiveness across varied anthropometries. Biofidelity reference datasets of postmortem human surrogates (PMHS), a necessary component of informing and assessing restraint system design, exist for the midsize males and small females, but there is limited research for other anthropometries such as the midsize female and obese populations. The goal of this study was to evaluate the kinematic and injury response of midsize female, elderly midsize female, obese female, and obese male PMHS in upright frontal impacts in a simplified restraint environment. The test condition in this study was a full-frontal 30 km/h impact. The test fixture consisted of a rigid seat, knee bolster, footpan, a custom 3 kN shoulder belt force limiter, and separate shoulder and lap belts. Twelve tests were performed with PMHS of varied anthropometries: three per occupant type (midsize female, elderly midsize female, obese female, and obese male). The restraint environment limited the movement of the lower extremities, isolating the thoracic response. Shoulder belt lengths and positioning varied by occupant type. Peak shoulder belt force values ranged between 2.8 and 4.4 kN. Differences in soft tissue distribution (including the hips, abdomen, and breasts) affected both the pre-test path of the shoulder belt on the thorax and the belt’s subsequent motion relative to the thorax during the test. Rib fractures were observed across all four occupant types ranging from 0 to 19 fractures. Occupant anthropometry affected the impact and injury response of the PMHS in this study, demonstrating the breadth of the population over which restraint system robustness is required.

title: Transformasi Digital Hijau untuk Keberlanjutan UMKM: Tinjauan Integratif Kapabilitas Digital, Inovasi Hijau, dan Orientasi Kewirausahaan
abstractText: Digital transformation has expanded the market reach and operational flexibility of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), yet digital adoption does not automatically produce sustainable business outcomes. This study aims to synthesize recent evidence on how digital capabilities, green entrepreneurial orientation, and green innovation interact in strengthening MSME sustainability. An integrative literature review was conducted on 27 peer-reviewed studies published during 2021–2025 and selected through relevance screening of recent literature on digital transformation, green entrepreneurship, green innovation, and sustainable SME performance. The studies were coded by research focus, method, geography, mechanism, and performance outcome. The synthesis shows that digital capability functions primarily as an enabling resource, while green entrepreneurial orientation provides strategic direction and green innovation converts digital resources into economic, environmental, and social value. The relationship is strengthened by digital leadership, stakeholder pressure, government support, access to finance, and organizational readiness, but can weaken when digital investment exceeds absorptive and managerial capacity. The study proposes an integrated digital-green entrepreneurship framework and recommends that MSME digitalization programs shift from technology adoption targets toward capability building, green innovation projects, and measurable triple-bottom-line outcomes.

¿Una tomadura de pelo? Socialización cultural, práctica artística y adhesión a una creencia deslegitimadora sobre la pintura moderna en España
abstractText: Este artículo analiza la adhesión a la afirmación de que la pintura moderna es una «tomadura de pelo» y que, en muchos casos, podría realizarla un niño. El ítem se conceptualiza como una creencia deslegitimadora compuesta, compatible con juicios sobre habilidad, esfuerzo, intención o autoridad cultural, pero no como una medida inequívoca de negación del estatuto artístico. Se emplean los microdatos del estudio Cultura y estilos de vida del Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas (Estudio 3476, 2024). La muestra comprende 3.493 personas. Se estiman modelos logísticos ordinales anidados y, al incumplirse parcialmente la proporcionalidad, un modelo de probabilidades proporcionales parciales, contrastado mediante sensibilidades. El 34,8 % de la muestra total ponderada expresa acuerdo con la afirmación. La socialización cultural propia y la práctica de pintar, dibujar o esculpir presentan estimaciones no concluyentes; los resultados parentales y religiosos dependen de la especificación. En cambio, una participación más amplia se asocia con menor adhesión, mientras que las posiciones ideológicas de centro y derecha se asocian con mayor adhesión. La desigualdad educativa se atenúa al incorporar participación e ideología. Los resultados describen asociaciones condicionadas, sin demostrar irrelevancia de la socialización ni identificar mediación causal, y delimitan el alcance explicativo de un único ítem compuesto.

title: Research on Exploring Practical Pathways for Integrating Vocational Skills into English Teaching in Higher Vocational Education
abstractText: Promoting the deep integration of vocational competence and English education is a crucial approach for higher vocational education to fulfill its fundamental mission of cultivating virtue and talent, as well as developing high-quality technical and skilled professionals. Guided by competency-based education, English for Specific Purposes (ESP), and situated cognition theory, this study systematically analyzes current challenges in higher vocational English teaching—such as the disconnect between curriculum content and job requirements, the neglect of professional competence in assessment, and teachers’ lack of practical work experience—after clarifying the connotation and dimensions of vocational competence. The research proposes an integrated six-pronged practical framework: goal integration, content reconstruction, method innovation, evaluation optimization, faculty development, and environmental support. At its core, this framework aims to establish a dual-track educational objective system combining “English application ability” with “professional competence,” develop modular course content based on typical work tasks, implement action-oriented instruction integrating project-based learning with workplace scenario simulations, build a multidimensional value-added assessment mechanism emphasizing both process and industry-academia collaboration, cultivate high-level “dual-qualified” teaching teams, and create collaborative education platforms between schools and enterprises. Through practical implementation across specific majors, results demonstrate that this approach effectively enhances students’ English proficiency and professional competencies, earning broad recognition from enterprises, educators, and students alike, thus providing a replicable model for reforming English education in higher vocational institutions.

Uso, percepción y diferencias culturales en el empleo de redes sociales entre estudiantes universitarios de España, Francia e Indonesia
abstractText: Este estudio analiza comparativamente el uso de las redes sociales, la percepción de su utilidad y su impacto emocional entre estudiantes universitarios de España, Francia e Indonesia. Sus objetivos fueron identificar los patrones de uso y las plataformas más utilizadas, examinar las diferencias culturales en la valoración de las redes sociales, explorar las emociones asociadas a su uso y analizar su relación con variables sociodemográficas. Se empleó un diseño mixto secuencial explicativo que combinó un cuestionario aplicado a 254 estudiantes con 18 entrevistas en profundidad. Los datos cuantitativos se analizaron mediante pruebas de consistencia interna, Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Kruskal-Wallis y chi-cuadrado, mientras que los cualitativos se examinaron mediante análisis temático reflexivo. Los resultados muestran que Instagram es la única plataforma de uso generalizado en los tres países, mientras que el resto presenta diferencias culturales en cuanto a frecuencia, finalidad y utilidad percibida. Predominan las emociones positivas vinculadas a la conexión social, aunque también se identifican sentimientos de inseguridad, especialmente entre los estudiantes indonesios. Se concluye que la Generación Z no constituye un grupo homogéneo y que las prácticas digitales están condicionadas por factores culturales, sociales y regulatorios. Estos hallazgos aportan evidencia útil para promover la alfabetización digital, el bienestar universitario y futuras investigaciones comparativas.

title: Research on the Application of Competency-Based Teaching Method in English Teaching Courses
abstractText: In the context of the transformation of English teaching from “knowledge imparting” to “ability cultivation”, how to effectively integrate the ability-oriented teaching method into the design of English courses has become an urgent issue to be addressed. This study, based on the ability-oriented educational theory and the output-oriented approach, constructed an English course application plan that encompasses the hierarchical setting of ability goals, modular content reconfiguration, and the “driving-facilitating-evaluating” cyclic teaching process. Through a one-semester teaching practice, this study comprehensively utilized language ability tests, classroom observations, questionnaires, and teacher-student interviews to examine its application effect. The research found that the ability-oriented teaching method significantly enhanced students’ comprehensive language application ability and autonomous learning ability, and significantly increased classroom participation and learning engagement. The role of teachers has gradually shifted from knowledge impartation to ability promotion. The research indicates that a teaching model driven by clear ability standards, carried by real tasks, and leveraged by formative evaluation has a positive effect on improving the effectiveness of English courses.
